h: Parents and Shabbos Reveal the Holiness of Body and Soul

p: "Every man shall fear his mother and his father,
and you shall keep My Shabbosos."
"It compares the fear of father and mother, etc.
it puts his mother before his father in fear,
while in honor it puts father before mother
(as they noted in the Gemara, Kiddushin 31a).
And the holy Zohar comes to explain
the order it gave in fear,
and because fear dwells in her,
and she is called 'the fear of Hashem,'
it put the fear of her first"
(and this is like the language of the holy Zohar
Now this needs to be understood:
of the fear of an actual mother
so what kind of answer is it
that the fear of the mother comes first
Nor is it an answer for
it put honoring the father first.
come to the son from the father.
And the mother, who is not obligated in Torah
she brings the fear of Hashem into the son,
שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת (מִשְׁלֵי לא, ל) אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה׳
for she is called "a woman who fears Hashem" (Mishlei 31:30).
And this is what the verse says (Mishlei 10:1):
and a foolish son is his mother's grief";
for the main wisdom of the son
and so the father is gladdened.
is one who has no fear of Heaven,
"'Why is there a price in the hand of a fool
to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart?' (Mishlei 17:16), etc.:
those who occupy themselves with Torah
and have no fear of Heaven";
for since he has no fear of Heaven,
he is nevertheless called a fool;
is that it teaches a person the way of Hashem,
and since he has no fear of Heaven
it is called "a price in the hand of a fool."
Therefore it writes: "and a foolish son"
who has no fear of Heaven
for she did not bring fear of Heaven into him.
And this is what it says:
and because fear dwells in her
and she is called 'the fear of Hashem,'
it put the fear of her first."
And there is an allusion to this in the Gemara too
the sound of his mother's footsteps,
he would say: Let me stand up
before the Shechinah that is coming."
for she brings the fear into his body,
and the Shechinah is called "the fear of Hashem,"
And in honor it put the father first,
and it says (Midrash Rabbah, Tetzaveh, Shemos Rabbah 38:5):
"We do not find honor with any of them
as it is written (Divrei HaYamim I 4:9):
'And Yaavetz was more honored than his brothers, etc.'
Why is honor written of him?
for he is Osniel ben Kenaz,
who restored the halachos that had been forgotten

(as they said in the sixth chapter of Avos, 6:3).
honoring the father before honoring the mother.
shares in the honor together with the father;

corresponding to the utterance "I am Hashem your God";
"Every man — his mother and his father, etc.,
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּמָרָה (שְׁמוֹת טו, כה)

"There He made for it a statute and an ordinance";
and it is expounded in the Mechilta (Beshalach, Vayassa 1):
as He commanded you at Marah."

which may be the general principle of the whole Torah

And in the holy Zohar (Beshalach, II 60a):
that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called Torah."
"a maidservant saw at the Sea, etc."
and afterward it departed from them,

that it is not that they were commanded
about keeping Shabbos and honoring parents,
for "and He spoke" is not written,
but rather that He set out the passages for them,
וְהַיְינוּ כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (שְׁמוֹת כא, א)
that you shall set before them";
that they would be commanded concerning the mitzvah of Shabbos.

a soul in which there is every perfection,

even the nations of the world practice,

of how Esav served his father, etc."

for the mitzvah of honoring parents?

do not ascribe grace to them";
and all the more so to praise Esav
But in truth this is not praise;
for among the nations of the world,
for whom the main thing is the body
and the pleasure of this world,
who brought them into this world,
This is not so with Yisrael:
that it would have been better for man not to have been created
and reason would not dictate honoring them
except because of the mitzvah of Hashem.

which is the honor of Hashem,

And the reason for the mitzvah of honoring one's father
is because they brought holiness into the body,
concerning the reason for the impurity of childbirth,
that it is because of the serpent's venom,
that even the most pious of the pious, etc.;
"And on the eighth day he shall be circumcised, etc.";
once he is circumcised he is called a tzaddik,
and so they have brought a tzaddik into the world
(as was explained in Parshas Tazria, maamar 5).
And this is why He set for them at Marah
that is, the body of a Jew
and for this reason there is a mitzvah of honoring parents,
for the holiness of the body
And this was given to them at Marah
so that they should not be distressed
lest, Heaven forbid, they become corrupted;
for the mitzvah of honoring parents indicates
that there is holiness in the body of a Jew,
indicates the holiness of the souls of Yisrael.
of which it says in the Midrash
